subject: Science
description: The human heart in section: four chambers, aorta and main vessels
alt: The human heart cut in half to show its four chambers (two atria on top, two ventricles below), the aorta and the main blood vessels
prompt: A front-view diagram of the human heart in section (patient's right is on the viewer's left). Four chambers: two smaller atria on top, two larger ventricles below, with the left ventricle wall thicker. The aorta arches from the top, with the pulmonary artery and the two venae cavae. Oxygen-rich side in the orange accent, the rest in blue and teal.
checklist: four chambers: two atria above, two ventricles below, separated by a septum
the left ventricle is larger with a thicker wall than the right
the aorta arches out of the left ventricle; the pulmonary artery leaves the right ventricle
the heart is oriented correctly: apex pointing down and to the viewer's right
